def-hh-coalgebra-and-coalgebra-map:
## Definition

Fix a field $k$ and use algebraic tensor products over $k$ as in [[def-hh-scalar-and-tensor-conventions]]. A **coalgebra** is a $k$-vector space $C$ with $k$-linear maps
$$
\Delta:C\longrightarrow C\otimes C,\qquad \varepsilon:C\longrightarrow k
$$
such that
$$\alpha_{C,C,C}\circ(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\circ\Delta=(\mathrm{id}_C\otimes\Delta)\circ\Delta$$
and
$$\lambda_C\circ(\varepsilon\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_C=\rho_C\circ(\mathrm{id}_C\otimes\varepsilon)\circ\Delta.$$
Here $\alpha$ is the tensor associator and $\lambda_C,\rho_C$ are the tensor unit isomorphisms. They are the maps supplied by [[lem-hh-tensor-coherence-on-elementary-tensors]] and [[def-hh-scalar-and-tensor-conventions]]. Thus the coassociativity equation has common target $C\otimes(C\otimes C)$; no unmentioned equality of differently parenthesized tensor spaces is assumed. The tensor products are algebraic, so each tensor is a finite sum of elementary tensors.

If $C,D$ are coalgebras, a **coalgebra map** $f:C\to D$ is a $k$-linear map satisfying
$$
\Delta_D\circ f=(f\otimes f)\circ\Delta_C,\qquad \varepsilon_D\circ f=\varepsilon_C.
$$
The equations say exactly that $f$ preserves comultiplication and counit.

The defining equations are properties; they do not assert existence for every vector space.
lem-hh-finite-spanning-list-contains-a-b:
## Statement

Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $k$, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ be a finite list spanning a subspace $W$. Some sublist of $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ is a basis of $W$. In particular, a subspace spanned by a finite list is finite-dimensional. No choice principle is used.
lem-hh-counit-uniqueness-and-finite-swee:
## Statement

For a fixed comultiplication $\Delta:C\to C\otimes C$, there is at most one counit. Also, Sweedler notation records a finite tensor sum, not a list of canonical summands: every contraction written from that notation must be the value of a well-defined linear map on the tensor.
def-hh-subcoalgebras-coideals-and-quotie:
## Definition

Let $(C,\Delta_C,\varepsilon_C)$ be a coalgebra. For every subspace $U\subseteq C$, write $j_U:U\hookrightarrow C$ for its inclusion and interpret the image of $U\otimes C$ or $C\otimes U$ in $C\otimes C$ through the tensor maps induced by inclusion.

A **subcoalgebra** of $C$ is a subspace $D\subseteq C$ equipped with linear maps $\Delta_D:D\to D\otimes D$ and $\varepsilon_D:D\to k$ satisfying the coalgebra axioms, such that the inclusion $j_D$ is a coalgebra map. Under AC, [[lem-hh-tensor-injections-quotients-and-kernels-over-a-field]] makes $j_D\otimes j_D$ and its iterated tensor powers injective. Hence the equivalent image criterion is that $\Delta_C(D)$ lie in the image of $D\otimes D$ and that the counit on $D$ be the restriction of $\varepsilon_C$: the inverse of $j_D\otimes j_D$ on its image gives the unique linear $\Delta_D$, and composing its axioms with the injective tensor powers reduces them to the coalgebra axioms on $C$.

A **coideal** is a subspace $I\subseteq C$ satisfying
$$\varepsilon_C(I)=0,\qquad \Delta_C(I)\subseteq \operatorname{im}(I\otimes C\to C\otimes C)+\operatorname{im}(C\otimes I\to C\otimes C).$$
Under AC the two tensor maps are injective, so the second condition is written in the standard shorthand $\Delta_C(I)\subseteq I\otimes C+C\otimes I$. Both conditions are part of the definition.

A **quotient coalgebra by $I$** means a coalgebra structure on the vector-space quotient $C/I$ for which the canonical projection $q:C\to C/I$ is a coalgebra map. The formula for that structure is not part of this definition.
lem-hh-finite-comatrix-coalgebra-exists:
## Statement

For a field $k$ and an integer $n\geq1$, let $E_n$ be the vector space with basis $c_{ij}$ for $1\leq i,j\leq n$. The linear maps defined on this basis by
$$\Delta(c_{ij})=\sum_{\ell=1}^n c_{i\ell}\otimes c_{\ell j},\qquad \varepsilon(c_{ij})=\delta_{ij}$$
make $E_n$ a coalgebra. In particular, the one-dimensional space with basis $c$ and maps $\Delta(c)=c\otimes c$, $\varepsilon(c)=1$ is a nonzero coalgebra.
def-hh-group-like-and-primitive-elements:
## Definition

Let $C$ be a coalgebra over $k$. An element $g\in C$ is **group-like** when
$$
\Delta(g)=g\otimes g,\qquad \varepsilon(g)=1.
$$
The counit condition excludes the zero vector and fixes the normalization.

Given a specified group-like element $g$, an element $x\in C$ is **primitive relative to $g$** when
$$
\Delta(x)=x\otimes g+g\otimes x,\qquad \varepsilon(x)=0.
$$
This is the $(g,g)$-skew-primitive condition. In a bialgebra with distinguished group-like unit $1$, the usual primitive condition is the special case $g=1$; an arbitrary coalgebra has no distinguished unit unless one is supplied.
thm-hh-coalgebra-quotient-and-kernel-des:
## Statement

Let $C$ be a coalgebra over a field $k$, and assume the Axiom of Choice. For every coideal $I\subseteq C$, the quotient vector space $C/I$ has a unique coalgebra structure making $q:C\to C/I$ a coalgebra map, given by
$$
\overline{\Delta}(c+I)=(q\otimes q)\Delta(c),\qquad \overline{\varepsilon}(c+I)=\varepsilon_C(c).
$$
This quotient has the universal property that every coalgebra map $f:C\to D$ with $I\subseteq\ker f$ factors uniquely through $q$ by a coalgebra map. Also, the kernel of every coalgebra map is a coideal, and the sum of any family of subcoalgebras of $C$ is a subcoalgebra.
thm-hh-fundamental-theorem-of-coalgebras:
## Statement

Let $C$ be a coalgebra over a field $k$. If $C$ is finite-dimensional, then every finite subset is contained in the finite-dimensional subcoalgebra $C$ itself, with no Choice assumption. For arbitrary $C$, assuming the Axiom of Choice, every finite subset $S\subseteq C$ is contained in a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra $D\subseteq C$.
